Case study
One short Friday, one Thursday off
Ida Lund works 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. Follow two dates in her November from her schedule to the booking page Reilly Barry opens.
Availability
Start from the weekly hours
Ida's Working hours schedule runs Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00. Under it, she clicks Add an override.
Date overrides
Pick a date and give it other hours
She picks Friday 20 November and moves the end time to 12:00. For that date, those hours replace her weekly ones.
Date overrides
Or take the day off
For Thursday 26 November she turns on Mark unavailable (All day). Nobody can book her that day.
Availability
Every change in one list
Both dates sit under Date overrides with their hours, ready to edit or delete. Once a date has passed, its override is archived on its own.
Booking page
Reilly sees the new hours
On Ida's booking page the 26th is greyed out and Friday the 20th offers times up to 11:30 only. Every other day keeps its 09:00 to 17:00.

Questions about date overrides
What an override changes, and what it leaves alone.
Ask a question
What's a date override?
A date on one of your availability schedules with its own hours. For that date, the override's hours replace your weekly hours, or the date is marked unavailable all day.
How is it different from out of office?
Out of office marks you away for a stretch of days, can show a note on your booking page and can send bookers to a teammate. A date override only changes the hours of one schedule on the dates you pick, and bookers just see those hours.
Can I add hours on a day I don't usually work?
Yes. An override replaces the day's weekly hours, so giving a Saturday 10:00 to 14:00 opens that Saturday even when your weekly hours leave weekends empty.
Can I override several dates at once?
Yes. Pick as many dates as you like in the month, and the hours you set apply to each of them. You can also add more than one time range to a date, such as a morning and a late afternoon.
Which event types does an override affect?
Every event type that uses the schedule you added it to. Event types on another schedule keep their own hours.
What happens to an override after its date?
Cal.com archives it automatically once the date has passed, so the list only shows the dates still ahead.
